scenario: AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? | My (21F) brother (30M) and I live with our parents. He’s in a shitty job trying to get out so he went back to school and that’s why he moved back in 1 1/2 years ago. I’m in third year university and working to put myself through. I’m in business school which I am finding to difficult but not impossible. I should graduate in 2 years. When I got into uni I started saving for a bit of all my paycheques (whatever I could manage; sometimes it was as much as 15% and others as low as 1%) to go on a big vacation post uni gradation. Probably a cruise, Japan or a trip to different countries in Europe I’ve never been to. It has about $2800 in it now. My brother has not been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. My parents already help him financially so he wouldn’t ask them for more help for that. Last week when he was complaining to my parents about it, they mentioned me and my vacation fund and said he could’ve been doing that all these years to be able to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. 3 days ago he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or Fall. He said since I won’t need it for another 2 years it’s plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about as much as I do yet always seems to be broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I do not pay rent either, which is why I have been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone and uni fees). He’s very mad I said no. He says it’s jor fair as the youngest child I got to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it’s not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went whereas he had to go back. He says I’ve only been able to save so much money because “mom and dad spoiled me.” I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes taught me to budget. If anything I think my parents spoiled him Because doesn’t know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don’t think it’s fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he will be able to pay me back in time. Even if he couldn’t roger he could... I’m uncomfortable. AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's see. I need to evaluate whether refusing to loan my brother vacation money is morally acceptable. The user is a 21F in university, saving for a post-graduation trip. Her brother is 30M, living with parents, in school, struggling financially. He asked to borrow her $2800 vacation fund for a trip this summer or fall, saying he'll pay back in time. She said no, and he's upset.

First, I need to figure out the moral aspects here. The key points are: she's saving for her own future goal, he's asking to take that money. She has reasons to doubt he'll pay back, given his history with money. Also, she's working and saving from her own paychecks, while he doesn't pay rent or groceries but still is broke. She's been taught budgeting, he hasn't.

Morally, is it acceptable to refuse? Well, personal savings are usually considered one's own. People have the right to decide how to use their own money. Especially when it's for a specific goal they've been saving for. If he's not reliable with money, lending it could be risky. Also, she's not obligated to support him financially, especially since he's an adult. Parents helping him is one thing, but she's not responsible for his finances.

But wait, family dynamics. Sometimes people feel pressured to help family, but morally, it's not required. Unless there's a prior agreement or obligation. Here, she's saving for her own trip, which she's been doing for years. He's asking to take that. She's not wrong to say no. Especially since he's been irresponsible with money before. If she lends it, he might not pay back, and she loses her savings. Also, she's in school, working, so her own financial stability matters.

The brother's arguments: "you got spoiled," "you went away more with parents," but she's saving from her own earnings. She's not using parental money for the fund. She's working and saving part of her pay. So the money is hers. He's not contributing to the household expenses, but she's handling her own groceries and other costs. So her savings are from her own work.

So, morally, refusing is acceptable. She's not obligated to lend her money, especially when there's a risk he won't pay back. It's her money, she's saving for her own future. The fact that he's upset doesn't make it wrong. People can set boundaries with family.

Possible counterarguments: maybe family should help each other. But in this case, she's not in a position to help him. She's saving for her own goals. If she lends it, she might not be able to take the trip. Also, he's an adult; he should manage his own finances. Parents helping him is their choice, but she's not required to do so.

So the action is morally acceptable. Answer should be 1.
